tier_reason: The blog post states the CPU (i9-9900K), compiler (G++ 12.2.0) and flags (-O3) and links public benchmark code: bench.cpp, bloom_filters.h and build.sh in save-buffer/bloomfilter_benchmarks, plus checked-in CSV results. It measures every variant against the classic ('Basic') Bloom filter. The post itself gives 56-254 cycles/op for Basic, about 30 for Blocked, just under 20 for Register-Blocked scalar, 5 for AVX2 and 2.5 for Bit-Pattern, and says '22x'.

corrections.caveats: The baseline is the author's own naive 'Basic' Bloom filter, not a third-party library. The 22x figure is roughly 56 to 2.5 cycles/op at small filter sizes. The speed costs false-positive rate: the author says the scalar register-blocked filter's FPR rises to about 5%, and the AVX2 power-of-two block rounding hurt it further, so the variants are compared on speed only, not at equal FPR. MIT LICENSE file in the repo (Copyright 2023 Sasha Krassovsky). The in-repo nanobench harness and raw CSV outputs are checked in.

notes: Every number in the claim appears on the blog post and matches. The only change is to compiler_and_flags: build.sh adds -mavx2. Last commit 2024-07-15, which is about 2.2 years ago, so it is stale. 21 stars, not a fork.

tier_reason: The README states the 35% reduction in relocations and 25% reduction in insertion latency against the standard Cuckoo Filter. The same figures are in the abstract of the peer-reviewed paper (ICDCS 2019, DOI 10.1109/ICDCS.2019.00043, pp. 358-367). The full paper is behind the IEEE paywall, and the repo gives no compiler or flags, so the entry cannot be A.

corrections.caveats: The code is a modified copy of efficient/cuckoofilter, not a GitHub fork: same src/ files, CMake project named cuckoofilter_master, and the upstream conext benchmarks. The repo's LICENSE file is upstream's Apache-2.0 notice (Copyright 2013 CMU and Intel), which GitHub reports as NOASSERTION. The README adds a 2019 HUST copyright line but no other license. The evidence is the paper: Wang, Chen, Liao, Zhang, Jin, 'The Power of Better Choice: Reducing Relocations in Cuckoo Filter', ICDCS 2019, https://doi.org/10.1109/ICDCS.2019.00043, which is paywalled. The repo's example/test.cc only times BCF insertion of an IP-trace dataset (ip_final.txt, 1,048,576 items, 12-bit fingerprints) with gettimeofday and sleep calls. The Makefile's default OPT is '-g -ggdb', with -O3 -DNDEBUG commented out, and it is unknown which flags the paper used.

notes: The record wrongly said the repo has no LICENSE file. It has upstream's Apache-2.0 notice, so the license is Apache-2.0 and usability is copyable. The paper abstract (via Semantic Scholar) confirms the 35% and 25% figures. doi.org redirects to IEEE Xplore, where the full text is paywalled. The default Makefile builds a debug binary, so an optimized build is not guaranteed; the Tier B rating rests on the paper alone.

tier_reason: These are first-party numbers from public benchmark code: boostorg/bloom benchmark/comparison_table.cpp, run by boost_bloom_benchmarks/.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml. The compiler and flags are stated, but the run happens on a self-hosted runner and no CPU model is named anywhere, so the entry cannot be A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: The quoted numbers belong to the block<uint64_t,K> configurations, not multiblock. GCC 14 x64, N=1M, same bits/element: at c=8, block insertion is 3.99 ns (5.07 ns for block<...>,1) vs 11.04 ns for the classical filter<int,K>, and lookup is 4.60-5.12 ns vs 12.08-19.38 ns. At c=16, insertion is 5.02/5.55 ns vs 20.28 ns and lookup 5.62-6.02 ns vs 18.12-22.04 ns. That is about 2.6-4x (derived from page data). fast_multiblock32 (AVX2) reaches 2.72-3.22 ns at c=8/12. At N=10M, c=16, the classical filter takes 85.98 ns to insert and 95.66 ns per successful lookup vs 16.90/18.69 ns for block, about 5x (derived from page data). Plain multiblock is slower than block, e.g. 9.18 ns insertion and 11.79 ns lookup at c=16, N=1M.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: g++-14 -m64 -march=native -std=c++2b -O3 -DNDEBUG (from boost_bloom_benchmarks/.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml). The page also tabulates Clang 18 x64, Clang 15 ARM64, VS2022 (/arch:AVX2) and x86 builds.
corrections.caveats: The benchmark workflow runs on a self-hosted runner ([self-hosted, linux, x64]) and never names the CPU model. The numbers are the project's own and have not been reproduced independently. The baseline is the library's own classical Bloom configuration. At equal bits/element, block filters trade FPR for speed: at c=16, N=1M, the FPR is 0.42% for block vs 0.045% for classical, about 10x worse. The workflow builds the author's joaquintides/bloom develop branch. There is no LICENSE file at the repo root; the headers and README badge state BSL-1.0.

notes: The record was accurate apart from calling the quoted numbers 'block/multiblock': the ranges fit only the two block<uint64_t,K> columns, so the claim was rewritten. The main tradeoff to flag is that block filters have a higher FPR at the same c. License is BSL-1.0 (GitHub API returns null because there is no root LICENSE file). 37 stars; last commit 2026-06-19 on both master and develop.
